Wrapped Texture Editor - test build
===================================

This build writes a crash report when it crashes.

Before you start: save your work and close any Wrapped Texture Editor that
is still open (also older copies). Then try the three ways of starting it
below, one after the other:

  1. "Wrapped Texture Editor.exe"            (normal start, Vulkan)
  2. "Start - DirectX 12.cmd"                (uses DirectX 12 instead of Vulkan)
  3. "Start - Vulkan without overlays.cmd"   (Vulkan, but without the OBS /
                                              Steam overlay hooks)

In each one, do what used to crash:
  - File > New from Model..., open an OBJ, glTF/GLB or FBX model, click Create
    (models without UVs now open too: the app generates a texture layout)
  - click "Split" (top of the view)
  - paint on the model for a bit, switch between 3D / 2D / Split

Note which of the three crash and which keep working.

Exporting layers (new in this build)
------------------------------------
  - Layers panel: Ctrl-click adds or removes a layer from the selection,
    Shift-click selects a range; a plain click selects just that layer.
  - Right-click a layer > "Export this layer..." (or "Export selected
    layers... (N)" with several selected): the Export dialog opens with
    Layers = "Selected (N)" and writes only those layers.
  - In File > Export..., tick "Pack into one .zip file" to get everything
    as one <name>.zip instead of loose files.

Objects (new in this build)
---------------------------
Open a model made of several parts, e.g. the chess set ABeautifulGame.glb,
or File > Open Sample > "Three Objects".
  - The side panel's "Objects" tab lists the parts. A click selects one,
    Ctrl-click adds or removes, Shift-click selects a range; a double-click
    selects it and moves the camera to it.
  - With the Navigate tool (top of the toolbar), a click on a part in the
    3D view selects it (a drag still turns the camera). Selected parts get
    a light blue tint while the Objects tab is open or Navigate is active.
  - The eye at the left of a row hides or shows that part. Hidden parts
    are not drawn, and painting, stamps and text go "through" them onto
    what is behind.
  - Keys: H = hide the selected parts, Shift+H = show only the selected
    parts (isolate), Shift+F = frame the selected parts, F = frame
    everything that is visible.
  - Alt+H = show everything again. Please check: does Windows beep or
    open a menu when you press Alt+H? (If it does, tell me; Ctrl+Shift+H
    would be the replacement.)
  - Save the project with a part hidden and open it again: the part is
    still hidden and a message says so. Undo is not affected by hiding.
  - Selecting a part never limits where you can paint.

Side panel tabs (new in this build)
-----------------------------------
  - The right panel now has two tab rows: on top Tool | Color |
    Texture sets | Objects, below Layers | Brush | Text.
  - The colour picker is on the "Color" tab. A click on the big colour
    square in the toolbar (left) opens that tab. Changing tools keeps
    the tab you chose.
  - Drag the line between the two groups to give one more room; a
    double-click on that line puts it back to automatic.
  - Close and restart the app: the tabs and the split you chose are kept.
  - Try a small window too (e.g. half the screen): nothing should overlap,
    the pages scroll.

Pen tablets (new in this build)
-------------------------------
With a drawing tablet or pen display (Windows Ink on in its driver):
  1. Hover over the model: the brush ring follows the pen and the status
     bar (bottom right) shows "Pen".
  2. Paint in 3D and in 2D, light to hard: the stroke goes thin to thick
     and the status bar shows the percentage. Fast curved strokes are
     smooth, not polygonal.
  3. Tap toolbar buttons, layer rows, tabs, sliders and menus with the
     pen: each tap is one click. Tooltips appear when hovering.
  4. Tool tab > Brush options > Pen pressure: turn Size off and Flow on:
     the width stays the same and the paint builds with pressure. Size on
     with "min 50 %": light strokes are half as wide.
  5. Turn the pen around: the tool switches to the Eraser and erases;
     turn it back: the previous tool returns.
  6. Hold the lower pen button and drag: 3D orbits, 2D pans; on a layer
     row it opens the row's menu.
  7. Press and hold the pen still on the model: no ring animation, no
     right-click menu, no ripple when you tap.
  8. Restart the app: the pressure settings are remembered.
  9. If the tablet driver's Windows Ink option is off: confirm there is no
     pressure (strokes stay full width), then Help > Tablet setup >
     Tablet input: WinTab, and check that pressure works and each stroke
     appears once. (Without a WinTab driver a message says Windows Ink is
     used.) Set it back to Windows Ink afterwards.
 10. Mouse painting feels and looks as before.
Please note the tablet model and driver version with anything that does
not work, and send the log (see below).

If it crashes
-------------
You should see a box "Wrapped Texture Editor crashed. A crash report was
saved to ...". The report is in the "crash" folder next to the exe:

  crash\crash-<numbers>.txt    (what happened, in plain text)
  crash\crash-<numbers>.dmp    (a small memory snapshot for debugging)

The log of the last run is here (paste this into Explorer's address bar):

  %APPDATA%\WrappedTextureEditor\log.txt

(If another copy of the app was open at the same time, the log is called
log-<number>.txt in the same folder instead.)

Please send the crash .txt file, the .dmp file next to it, and the log.
The log is overwritten every time the app starts, so copy it before
starting the app again.

If nothing crashes, the log of that run is still useful: it lists which
graphics backend was used and which overlay programs were hooked in.
